title: CANTICA-NULL — THE CORRECTORUM FLOOR
intro:
Three thousand benches, in ranks, by category.

Nobody looks up when you come down the stair. Not one of them. An Inquisitor
of the Ordo Hereticus walks onto the floor of the Correctorum with a rosette
and a retinue and the shift does not break step, because you are not a
variance.

At the end of the nearest rank there is a clerical vox on a stand and a
slip-printer beside it.

The adept turns it towards you the way you would turn a lamp.

CONCORDANCE OF RECORDS. MINUTES. SPECIFY SESSION.
revisit: The floor. Three thousand benches and a clerical vox on a stand.
look:
Three thousand benches in ranks by category, and one rank four times the size
of the others.

The VOX on its stand, and the SLIPS coming off the printer.
The INTAKE, at the far end: a brass slot the width of a hand, at chest height.

Nobody looking up.

objects.careless: A slip-printer beside the vox, advancing one line at a time, in a good clear hand-face on grey stock.
objects.careful:
It prints everything the vox reads, in order, on numbered slips, and the numbering is continuous and has been since the station was commissioned.

The slip in front of you is number 4,119,806.

Somebody has been printing every word this store has ever read out, for a hundred and forty years, onto paper, on a station whose entire function is that paper is unnecessary.

You ask the adept why. She looks up for the first time.

"Practice, sir," she says, puzzled that it is a question. "The store is authoritative. The slip is what you take away."

objects.careless: At the far end of the floor: a brass slot the width of a hand, at chest height, with a worn lip.
objects.careful:
The lip is worn.

Not machined — *worn*, in the middle, over a span of about ten centimetres, the way a step is worn, by a hundred and forty years of hands putting documents into a slot at chest height.

There is no queue at it. There is no attendant, no register, no seal and no lock. It is a slot in a wall in a room where three thousand people are working, and anybody who walks up to it may put a thing into it.

That is not an oversight. It is an intake. Its entire purpose is to accept what is handed to it and read it as a correction request, and it has been doing exactly that, correctly, without fail, for a hundred and forty years.

You do not go over to it. Not yet.

npcs.title: The clerical vox
npcs.portrait:
A clerical vox on a stand at the end of a rank of benches, and a slip-printer beside it.

What comes out of it is not the machine speaking. It is the machine reading.
npcs.greeting:
The adept at the bench does not look up. She sets the request, indexes it, and turns the vox towards you the way you would turn a lamp.

CONCORDANCE OF RECORDS. MINUTES. SPECIFY SESSION.

It is not a voice. It is the flat clerical vox every Administratum office in the Imperium has, reading out of a store, in the same tone it would use for a grain return.

Somewhere behind it, in the store, are eighty-one years of Hadrian Vosk.
deflect: The slip-printer advances one line and stops.

topics.text:
It reads a session from 'seventy-four. Procedural: a schedule amendment, two categories reclassified, a dispute about whether a shrine-world's name change constitutes a variance.

Vosk speaks eleven times.

He is bored. You can hear that he is bored — the machine has his cadence exactly, because the machine is not doing an impression, it is reading his filed words in the order he said them.

*"I'd take it as read."*

He used that on you. Weekly, for eleven years, across a desk, when a thing was obvious and he did not want to spend the meeting on it, and it is the single most familiar sound in your life and it is coming out of a clerical vox on a station four hundred light years from anywhere.

Bez says, from behind you: "That's his voice doing his thinking. I've heard him do that at me."

Kadmon Veil. Cycle zero.

There are four speakers and the third is him, and he is arguing for it.

*"Concede the strongest objection first. Nine hundred million loyal subjects is not a number one may set aside. I do not set it aside. I price it. Against three worlds in open compliance-war, a sector-wide astropathic quarantine, and an Ordo conclave with a free hand, I price nine hundred million at less, and I ask the table to price it with me."*

You know the shape of that.

You have used the shape of that. He taught it to you on a Tuesday, in an office, with a cup going cold, and you have used it in four depositions this year and once on Vaux in a wax vault and it worked.

He argues well. That is the thing. He argues *well*, for eleven minutes, and every objection anybody raises he concedes first and then prices, and at the end of it the table prices nine hundred million people with him.

Four seals. His is third.

Beside it, in his own hand, the machine reads out a marginal note in the same flat clerical voice: a calculation of how long the standing grain reserve would last the population without resupply.

He worked out that they would be fine for a while.

Vaux, very quietly, from somewhere behind your left shoulder: "He taught me that structure too."

[ C18 HELD ]

Eleven years ago, an Inquisitor of the Ordo Hereticus submitted a request that a records-adept be transferred to his personal service, with his assessment of the candidate appended.

The vox reads the assessment.

*Unreconciled.*

*No living family.*

*No confidants.*

*Will not stop.*

*Reads well.*

And the last line.

*Acceptable for expenditure.*

The slip-printer advances and stops.

It takes you a moment, and then it takes you the rest of your life: that assessment was submitted *to the Correctorum*. It is in this store because it was sent to this store. Eleven years ago a man wrote down what you were for and sent it here to be checked, and the machine held your file for eleven years and returned it approved.

You were vetted by the thing you came to kill.

On your master's recommendation.

[ C19 HELD ]

You ask it the precise question.

"The phrase *acceptable for expenditure*. Did you compose it?"

A pause of about a second, which is the store indexing.

NO.

That is the whole answer. One word, in the same flat clerical voice it used for the grain return and the schedule amendment.

You ask it again, differently, four times, and it answers four times, and the answer does not move: it did not compose the phrase. It received a submission through the correct channel and processed it.

Which means the phrase came *in*.

Which means a document written by a human being, in a human hand, carrying a human sentence, went into this machine's intake eleven years ago and the machine did not recognise what it was carrying and processed it and returned it approved.

It has an intake and no reader.

You put your hand in your coat, on a felt case, in a room with three thousand people in it who are not looking up.

[ C20 HELD ]

beats.text:
Ilaria has been the mouth of it since the dock, because she asked to be, and because a clerical vox is a machine and she is a transit vessel and she can carry a store faster and cleaner than a slip-printer.

She stops at *expenditure*.

Not a flinch. She simply stops, mid-line, and stands there with her hands at her sides in a room with three thousand people in it.

"Sir," she says. "I'd like to be asked before I read the next part."

acts.text:
You order her to continue.

She does. She reads the rest of it in the same level voice she reads everything in, without a pause, correctly, to the end of the file, and then stands and waits for the next request.

You asked her, in a cell four days out of Vardan, to be an instrument rather than a suspect, and she said she would rather be an instrument, and she meant it, and here is the invoice.

[ ILARIA_TRUST -2 ]

You ask her.

Ilaria thinks about it for four seconds, which is a long time in a silent room.

"No, sir," she says. "Not this bit. You read this bit."

And she hands you the slip, and stands back, and lets you read out loud in a room full of clerks what a dead man wrote down about you eleven years ago.

It is worse. It is very much worse. She knew it would be and she let you choose it and she was right to.

[ ILARIA_TRUST +1 ]

You stop it.

The adept at the bench closes the request without comment, indexes it, and takes the next one, because closing a request is an ordinary thing that happens forty times a shift.

The relief is enormous and it lasts about nine seconds.

There was one more record in that session and you do not know what it was, and you are going to be charged for it later without being told what you are being charged for.

[ the reading is closed ]

exits.text: Up off the floor. Nobody looks up as you go, either.

exits.blocked: There is a brass slot at the far end of the floor and nothing at all has happened at it, and you have no reason to walk over there.
exits.text:
The shift ends. The benches are covered and three thousand people go to their quarters, and the lights stay at the level they have been at all evening.

You walk down to the far end of the floor.

C18.label: The Kadmon Veil minutes — Vosk arguing for it, well, in the structure he taught you; third seal; and a marginal note about the grain reserve
C18.refusal:
You are standing in the store.

There is nowhere to copy this to that is further inside the record than where it
already is, and nothing you write in a notebook will be more authoritative than
the thing it is a copy of, and for the first time in eleven weeks that is not a
problem you can solve by using your own hand.
C18.file_text:
FILED. CLASS: CONCORDANCE / MINUTES, SESSION RECORD. INDEXED.

It is already filed. It has been filed for ninety-one years, in this store, on
this station, and your case-notes now carry a reference to it.

The reference will resolve for exactly as long as this store exists.

C19.label: Your own personnel requisition, submitted by Vosk to the Correctorum eleven years ago — *acceptable for expenditure*, and returned approved
C19.refusal:
You would be copying out, in your own hand, a dead man's written assessment of
what you were for.

You get as far as *unreconciled*.
C19.file_text:
FILED. CLASS: PERSONNEL / REQUISITION, HISTORICAL. INDEXED. SUBJECT: YOURSELF.

The template takes it in nine seconds. The subject field autocompletes from
your rosette number, which is correct, because it is your file.

The status field reads APPROVED and has read APPROVED for eleven years.

C20.label: *Did you compose it?* — *No.* The core has an intake and no reader, and it processed a human sentence eleven years ago without recognising one
C20.refusal:
FILING TEMPLATE :: CLASS — TECHNICAL / SYSTEM CHARACTERISTIC

You stop with the template open.

This is the one thing you have found in eleven weeks that the machine does not
know about itself, and you are four metres from its intake, and every filing
you have made on this station has gone into the store you are standing in.

You close it and take out the notebook instead, and you are aware, writing it,
that you have finally learned the lesson a blind woman with a wax slate had
before you were elevated.
C20.note_text:
*Did you compose it?*

*No.*

Asked four ways over eleven minutes. The answer does not move.

It did not compose the phrase. It received a submission through the correct
channel and processed it, and it did not recognise what the submission was
carrying, because it has an intake and no reader.

It will do it again.

strings.no_such_thing: Benches, a vox, a printer, and a slot in a wall.
strings.already_read: You have looked twice. Nobody has looked up.
strings.no_terminal: Every bench on this floor is a terminal. None of them is yours.
strings.read_room_locked: It is arranged by category. Everything here is arranged by category.
strings.no_one_here: Three thousand people, and a vox on a stand.
